summary.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 volume of 745,000 tons was below expectations, down roughly 20% QoQ, driven by the UAE disruption (about 25,000 tons lost QoQ), weak SG Premium volumes against secondary steel, an energy crisis hitting rust-proof pipes and roofing (25,000-30,000 tons), and destocking after steel prices rose. Gross profit per ton rose INR1,000 QoQ as management held prices, and EBITDA per ton was flat at above INR5,500. Management says July volumes were up about 20% MoM at over 300,000 tons, and it reiterated 15-20% volume growth and above 20% absolute EBITDA growth for FY27. Working capital days remain below zero and cash was about INR14 billion at June end versus INR15 billion in March 2026.

segments.name: Apollo branded products
segments.commentary: Management targets EBITDA of INR6,000-7,000/ton for Apollo and roofing products combined; the company is at that range currently. Primary and secondary volumes were hit by high prices and channel destocking.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Priced about 6-7% below APL Apollo brand at around INR58,000/ton; EBITDA spread INR0-1,000/ton depending on micro-market. Volumes fell due to the primary-secondary price gap (INR10-12/kg currently).

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: Dubai volumes fell to 5,000-6,000 tons/month during the disruption; July output was 10,000-12,000 tons, with a target of 16,000-17,000 tons in August and 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up. Management expects UAE EBITDA to reach INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds.

segments.name: Roofing products
segments.commentary: Hit by the energy crisis in India (25,000-30,000 tons lost). Management says roofing EBITDA is currently INR6,000-7,000/ton, with a roofing line starting in APL adding about 20,000 tons of ramped-up volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management says 15% is achievable with confidence and 20% needs tailwinds.
FY27 absolute EBITDA growth of 20% or more; FY27 EBITDA per ton expected in the INR5,000-5,500 range.
Quarterly targets: Q2 about 1.0 million tons, Q3 about 1.05 million tons, Q4 about 1.2 million tons. Monthly targets: August 325,000-335,000 tons, September 350,000-360,000 tons.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1 in volume and absolute EBITDA; H2 expected to outperform H1.

Long term: value-added share to rise from about 65% to 75-80% by Q4 FY28; EBITDA per ton target of INR6,000 for the 8 million ton base over the next 2-3 years; ROCE target to return to 30% and then 40%.

Gorakhpur (200,000 tons) expected to start around September 2026; Siliguri (300,000 tons) in Q4 FY27; Malur (about 1 million tons, value-added, EBITDA target INR8,000+/ton) in July-October 2027; a 0.5 million ton plant planned in Maharashtra or North Karnataka. About 2 million tons of new capacity is due over about 2.5 years, plus 1 million tons via debottlenecking.
capex_capacity: Total capex plan of 7 million tons. Gorakhpur 200,000 tons (start around September 2026), Siliguri 300,000 tons (Q4 FY27), Malur about 1 million tons (July-October 2027), a 0.5 million ton plant in Maharashtra or North Karnataka, plus 1 million tons from debottlenecking.
The Bhuj plant was dropped; the Mumbai plant is being shifted fully to exports. A new 500,000-ton plant near the Pune corridor is planned to cut freight to INR200-300/ton from INR1,100-1,200/ton.
Current capacity is about 5 million tons, with full operation targeted in Q4 FY27.
Solar segment: management expects 4-5% of total volume from solar products within 2-3 years, versus a low current contribution.
demand_pricing: Q1 disruption drivers: UAE loss (~25,000 tons QoQ), SG Premium share loss to secondary steel, energy crisis in India, and destocking by channel partners after steel prices rose INR7,000-8,000/ton in Q4 FY26.
July demand recovered as the price correction ended; dealers returned to normal stock positions and July volume was over 300,000 tons (about 20% MoM).
Pricing: management says it held prices, passing on steel price increases plus INR100-200/ton. Price cuts of INR100-200/ton were applied to about 15-20% of the portfolio to gain volume.

Competition: management says it is not losing share, targeting 60-65% share of its market, and sees Tata's planned 4-5 million ton pipe capacity as unclear by segment. Primary steel capacity additions (Lloyd, AM/NS, JSW, Tata, JSPL) are expected to narrow the primary-secondary gap over 1-3 quarters.
PEB segment: about 20% of PEB structure weight is steel pipe; APL holds a 65-70% share with large PEB players.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 volume guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA growth of 20%+ still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% volume growth and 20%+ EBITDA growth; 15% is considered confident, and 20% needs tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE outlook and how will the company participate in reconstruction demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai volume recovered to 10,000-12,000 tons in July, with a target of 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up.

qa_highlights.question: How is competitive intensity with Tata and others evolving, and how is market share protected?
qa_highlights.answer: No share loss seen so far; the target is to hold 60-65% share. Tata's pipe plans are not clearly defined by segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton path beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads expected to be INR5,000-5,500/ton in FY27, improving INR100-200/ton a year, with a target of INR6,000/ton at 8 million tons in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise YoY despite lower volume?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2025 repositioning of APL Apollo brand raised prices by about INR500/ton, which lifted spreads from Q4 FY25 through FY26 and into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were the segment-level EBITDA targets, and why were segment margins no longer disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Apollo and roofing are targeted at INR6,000-7,000/ton, SG Premium at about INR500/ton, and UAE at INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds. Management stopped segment margin disclosure to avoid competitor scrutiny.

risks_watch: Volume ramp-up: H2 needs about 3.5-4 lakh tons per month, and any shortfall would make the 15% volume target difficult.
Primary-secondary steel gap: if it persists for 1-3 more quarters, SG Premium and secondary-linked volume stays under pressure.
UAE: raw material shortage for about 70,000 tons, high demurrage costs, and pricing hits in the post-disruption recovery.
Gorakhpur (September) and Siliguri (Q4 FY27) timing; Malur (July-October 2027) execution risk on the 7 million ton capex plan.
Possible pricing pressure from the 15-20% of the portfolio where prices were cut; the EBITDA per ton could drop INR100-200 in some quarters.
Employee cost step-up in Q1 that management says will reverse once volumes recover.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance and disclosed no segment EBITDA going forward, reducing visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance and the recovery in July, but cautious on quarterly volume, which management says is hard to forecast. Answers on UAE, segment margins, and FY28 were less specific, and management said it would not give FY28 guidance.
